A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BWFlow research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendices F, H, and I report original BWFlow experiments on graph and molecule generation, including benchmark results and ablations.

after.justification: The original BWFlow benchmark and ablation results remain, with additional DisCo comparisons and a QM9 interpolation-path analysis.

M1.justification: The GraphMRF representation, BW interpolation, velocity formulas, and continuous/discrete algorithms remain unchanged. Algorithms 1–2 move into the main text; the proposed future use of MRF-space velocity learning is not an implemented method change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Planar, Tree, SBM, COMM20, MOSES, GUACAMOL, QM9, and GEOM, retaining the molecular variants. The added QM9 trajectory analysis uses existing dataset and task coverage.

E2.justification: DisCo joins the controlled, averaged Planar and SBM comparisons in Tables 1 and 12. Although v3 already includes DisCo in best-checkpoint and molecule comparisons, its participation in these particular comparisons is new.

E3.justification: Section 4.2 replaces the description of EMA over checkpoint results with ordinary last-five-checkpoint averaging and EMA applied to the model; this reported revision does not establish reruns. Figure 6c adds negative atom validity measured across QM9 interpolation times. Table 10 settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The training-path analysis expands from Planar and Tree in v3 Figure 5 to include QM9 in v4 Figure 6, testing how atom validity evolves under linear versus BW interpolation. The Tree trajectory is also revised. Existing LSQR, interpolation, convergence, and reduced-sampling-step analyses remain.

E5.justification: Section 4.2 and Table 1 distinguish checkpoint averaging, now called CAVG, from model EMA, refining the statistical aggregation description. Table 12 retains five sampling repetitions of 40 graphs and mean/standard-deviation reporting; no additional runs or seeds are established.

E6.justification: Tables 1 and 12 add DisCo results, including V.U.N. of 57.5±2.5 on Planar and 55.0±5.9 on SBM. Figure 6 adds QM9 trajectories and replaces the Tree curves: the BW peak changes from approximately 315 in v3 Figure 5b to approximately 30. Existing main BWFlow scores remain unchanged. The unexplained Tree revision does not establish a same-setting performance gain.

T1.justification: Appendix A.2 adds a short chain-rule and conditional-independence derivation supporting the existing GraphMRF factorization. This is a limited addition to its formal justification; the BW distance, interpolation, and velocity propositions and their principal proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: GraphMRF-based BW interpolation supports graph generation with competitive performance, improved training dynamics, and efficient sampling. Added explanations and evidence do not redefine those contributions.

C2.justification: Section 3.1 and Appendix A.3 add a latent-generative-model interpretation of low-frequency emphasis and suggest future MRF-space velocity learning with KL divergence. A new introduction footnote qualifies the transition near t=0.8 as empirical and dataset-dependent. Existing Tree, computational-cost, and multi-relation limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix I.5 newly identifies SBM as the source for Figure 1a and explicitly discloses that its green ideal path is synthetically constructed for illustration. Hardware, timing information, and configurations in Tables 9–10 remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix A.3 adds connections to latent generative research citing Osman et al. (2025), Siraudin and Morris (2026), and Park et al. (2023). Appendix G.1 replaces an unresolved citation with Haviv et al. (2024). The broader research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: Changes include localized explanatory rewrites, terminology and cross-reference corrections, author-name and affiliation edits, acknowledgements, and a new LLM-use disclosure in Appendix J. The main narrative and existing appendix organization are largely retained.

P2.justification: The two-column main text becomes a single-column ICLR layout, extensively reflowing and relocating figures, tables, equations, and algorithms. v4 also adds the GraphMRF diagram in Figure 4 and notation Table 18, expands the training-path figure, and revises its Tree plot and legends.

improvement.justification: The explicit synthetic-path disclosure and expanded GraphMRF explanation improve transparency, while the DisCo comparison and QM9 trajectory provide limited additional support. These gains outweigh small drawbacks, including Table 18 calling Λ a covariance although Equation 8 uses Λ†, and the unexplained Tree-curve revision. The core method and main performance evidence remain stable.
